text.p: Italian debt markets ended with mild gains, still propelled forward by optimism over European convergence but held slightly in check ahead of preliminary consumer prices data due at 1530 GMT.
The February 2007 Btp wound the spread over the benchmark Bund into another record low of 118 basis points and closed 15 basis points up at 99.37, with the actual yield 6.94 percent.
The September BTP future on LIFFE was 15 basis points higher at 133.46.
Dealers said the market was now awaiting preliminary inflation data from a further six sample Italian cities.

Five cities' data released on Friday indicated inflation running at 1.5 percent year on year for June. If confirmed by today's data, this will be the lowest level of inflation for 30 years. Analysts had forecast inflation at 1.5-1.6 percent year on year after May's 1.6 percent.
Few in the market expect a cut near term in the 6.75 percent discount rate but as one trader said: "You can't rule it out."
The lira gave up earlier gains against the mark to be quoted at 977.80/8.10 per mark compared with 976.60 earlier.
